analysis.title: The Point for North America, Thursday, 22 October 2026
key_insights: Abbott 3Q26 was below expectations on softer EP and Diabetes revenue. Abbott announced plans to spin out its Nutrition franchise, expected by YE27. Revenue was $13.01B (up 7.0% comparable) vs FactSet consensus $12.99B, and EPS $1.42 matched consensus. Management lowered 2026 revenue growth to about 6.0%. Citi rates ABT Buy and cuts TP to $122 from $125.

Intuitive Surgical 3Q26 beat on revenue ($3.05B, up 22% y/y vs $2.91B consensus) and EPS ($3.00 vs $2.65 consensus), but da Vinci procedures grew 14% y/y (US +10%, OUS +20%), missing the procedure bogey that investors watch. Guidance points to the 14.5% midpoint. Gross margin rose to 69.9% from 68.0%. Citi rates ISRG Buy.

Meta: Citi is incrementally positive after 3Q26, citing an AI product cycle. 10M users have set up a Muse agent, about 25% return daily, and shopping is the most common use case. IG and FB Reels time spent per user hit all-time highs and 4Q revenue guidance was better than expected. 2027 stays an investment year. Buy reiterated, TP raised to $905.

IBM 3Q26: headline revenue grew 6% y/y in constant currency vs Street 3%, led by infrastructure and software. Software grew 9%. Under the surface, Automation declined low single digits, consulting disappointed, and organic software demand looks challenged. FY revenue guide of 4-5% was reaffirmed, FCF guidance raised. Citi lifts PT to $280.

Cloudflare preview: at about 30x EV/Sales 2027 it is one of the most expensive names Citi covers (CRWD 32x, DDOG and PANW about 17x). Fresh checks support 2H acceleration. Citi's bull case is 35%+ durable topline growth into and beyond CY27 vs Street 28%. Developers passed 10M in 3Q26. Buy reaffirmed, $400 PT.

Everpure (P): after a small-group meeting with the CTO, management reports no meaningful change in demand trends despite macro concerns about AI spending, citing enterprise, hyperscaler and neocloud demand. Citi stays constructive.

Palantir preview: Citi expects upside in US Government and Commercial despite tougher comparisons, with positive intra-quarter checks and a federal rebound. The stock is up 50% since last quarter vs IGV up 10%. Buy reiterated, estimates raised above Street, TP raised to $250.

Lam Research: Citi expects outperformance vs the wafer fab equipment (WFE) market in 2027 on etch and deposition intensity, but warns against raising 2027/28 WFE expectations above Citi's $224B/$286B because of supply shortages (gas delivery components, DRAM, MLCC, PCB boards, magnets). FY27/28/29 EPS raised 4%/5%/5%. TP moves to $435 from $450 on a 33x P/E vs 36x prior.

Danaher 3Q26: 4Q26 revenue guided up about 3% on respiratory softness (consensus 5.2%) and EPS about $2.48 (vs $2.59). FY26 core growth of 2.5% falls below the prior 3-4% commentary, yet FY26 EPS guidance rose to $8.57-$8.62 on better margins. Early FY27 color is core growth of 4-5% ex-respiratory. Buy, TP raised to $270 from $230.

Wabtec 3Q: adj. EPS $2.83 (+22% y/y) beat Citi $2.75 and consensus $2.73. The 2026 adj. EPS guide was raised to $10.85-11.05 while the revenue guide was held at $12.30-12.60B. Organic revenue missed on equipment deliveries slipping from 3Q to 4Q. Multi-year backlog rose 2% q/q. Shares were up 1% mid-day. TP cut to $334 from $338.
Exelon holds in-the-money interest rate swaps, which lower near-term refinancing risk. Pending items are Pennsylvania election results and the final Illinois (ICC) order in December.

Hasbro shares rose about 11% after results beat across the P&L and every segment. Magic sales accelerated vs a strong 2Q. The 4Q guide looked soft only because of a shipment timing shift. TP raised to $137 from $117, Buy.

Knight-Swift 3Q adj. EPS $0.83 beat Citi $0.72 and Street $0.76 and the company's own $0.71-0.77 range. 4Q adj. EPS guide of $0.78-0.84 compares with Street in line. Truckload adjusted operating ratio is guided to improve 650-750bp y/y. This contrasts with JBHT and WERN, which posted disappointing 3Q results. KNX remains Citi's top truckload pick.

Pegasystems 3Q26 missed core metrics and lowered ACV growth, but had its best new ACV quarter of the year (+$33M q/q). Headcount is expected to fall about 5% into 2027. Buy reiterated, TP cut to $50 from $52.

Bank OZK: core results were softer than expected, the guide implies continued net interest margin compression, and 2027 PPNR (pre-provision net revenue) guidance looks below consensus. Citi sees growing pressure in multifamily and expects 2027 credit pressure to match or exceed 2026. Sell rating and $40 TP maintained.

Integra LifeSciences 3Q26 revenue of $411.2M (+2.5% organic) matched pre-announced results. Tissue Reconstruction faces unanticipated competitive and execution headwinds. 2026 revenue guide of $1.634B-$1.654B sits below the $1.66B consensus. Management still expects growth in 2027. Neutral/High Risk, TP to $14 from $15.

Transports weekly: CSX, KNX, UNP, NSC, UPS and WERN report 3Q26 over the coming week. Citi estimates are slightly below Street for UNP ($3.40 vs $3.47), CSX ($0.52 vs $0.53), NSC ($3.39 vs $3.47) and KNX ($0.72 vs $0.76). UNP 3Q volumes are running +5.7% y/y per AAR data.

A&D chart of the day: SPCX management sees YE27 ARR of $500B-$1T as possible, which Citi says could exceed the 2027 consensus revenue of its entire A&D coverage. The driver is monetization of data center capacity.
Airlines chart of the day: premium revenue trends are still accelerating even as some travel segments decelerate. Citi attributes this to supermajors' strategy of raising premium seating share.

US Digital Assets: Citi views the OCC's final rule implementing the GENIUS Act as an incremental positive for stablecoins. The OCC dropped language that could have constrained issuer-distributor arrangements and chose case-by-case review. Citi sees regulated issuers such as Circle, distribution platforms such as Coinbase, and banks as the main beneficiaries. AML, sanctions and Treasury guidance remain outstanding.

Sector flows: Citi's flow model favors Tech, Communications and Health Care on a two-month view, with Financials, Consumer Discretionary and Utilities as the largest shorts. In the latest week, long-only and hedge fund managers turned decisively against Tech, in line with an AI-related selloff over data center financing and capex vs slower AI revenue. Sector returns now point Citi's regime model toward Tightening Financial Conditions and Stagflation readings instead of Goldilocks.

earnings_insights: ABT 3Q26: revenue $13.01B (up 7.0% comparable) vs FactSet consensus $12.99B, reported. EPS $1.42 (up 9%) vs consensus $1.42. Operating margin 23.4% vs 23.0% y/y. 2026 revenue growth guidance lowered to about 6.0%.

ISRG 3Q26: revenue $3.05B (up 22% y/y) vs FactSet consensus $2.91B, reported. EPS $3.00 (up 25.1%) vs consensus $2.65. Gross margin 69.9% vs 68.0% y/y, operating margin 41.6% vs 39.0%. Procedure growth guide midpoint now 14.5% vs prior 13.5-15.5% range.
META 3Q26 reported. Citi says 4Q revenue guidance came in better than expected. 2027 is an investment year.
IBM C3Q26: revenue up 6% y/y constant currency vs Street 3%, reported. Software up 9%. FY revenue guide of 4-5% reaffirmed, FCF guidance lifted.

DHR 3Q26 call: 4Q26 revenue guided up about 3% (FactSet consensus 5.2%), EPS about $2.48 (vs $2.59 prior). FY26 core growth 2.5%, FY26 EPS guided to $8.57-$8.62 from $8.45-$8.60. FY27 initial commentary core growth 4-5% ex-respiratory, respiratory $1.5B flat y/y.

WAB 3Q: adj. EPS $2.83 reported vs Citi $2.75 and consensus $2.73 estimates. 2026 adj. EPS guide $10.85-11.05 (midpoint $10.95 vs prior Citi/consensus estimates $10.88/$10.87). Revenue guide kept at $12.30-12.60B vs prior Citi/consensus $12.57B estimates.

KNX 3Q: adj. EPS $0.83 reported vs Citi $0.72 and Street $0.76 estimates, above guidance of $0.71-0.77. Total revenue $2,201M. 4Q adj. EPS guide $0.78-0.84 (midpoint $0.81 vs Citi $0.76 estimate). 4Q Truckload adj. OR guide 85.4%-86.4% vs Citi 88.5% and Street 87.6% estimates. LTL adj. OR guide 93.1%-94.1% vs Citi 93.1% and consensus 92.7%.
HAS 3Q: outpaced all expectations across the P&L and each segment, per Citi. Shares up about 11% on Tuesday. 4Q guide implied weakness only because of a shipment timing shift.
PEGA 3Q26: missed core metrics but best new ACV quarter of the year (+$33M q/q). Targets $700M 2028 FCF.

IART 3Q26: revenue $411.2M (+2.5% organic), in line with pre-announced $410-$412M. Adj. EBITDA $79.8M vs consensus $83.0M. EPS $0.59 (up 9% y/y). 2026 revenue guide $1.634B-$1.654B vs consensus $1.66B, EPS $2.30-$2.40 vs consensus $2.40.
OZK: core results softer than expected, NIM compression guided, 2027 PPNR guidance appears softer than consensus.
Upcoming 3Q26 reports over the next week: CSX, KNX, UNP, NSC, UPS, WERN. Citi/consensus adj. EPS estimates: UNP $3.40/$3.47, CSX $0.52/$0.53, NSC $3.39/$3.47, KNX $0.72/$0.76.
NET and PLTR 3Q26 results are previewed, not yet reported. Citi expects strong upside at PLTR in US Government and Commercial and a steady acceleration at NET.
crypto_views: Citi views the OCC's final rule implementing the GENIUS Act as an incremental positive for stablecoins, giving clarity on issuance, reserves, redemptions, custody and supervision without a more restrictive approach to stablecoin rewards programs.
The OCC removed proposed language that could have constrained issuer-distributor arrangements and opted for case-by-case review, preserving flexibility for exchanges and fintech platforms.

Citi sees Circle (regulated issuer), Coinbase (distribution platform) and banks entering stablecoins as the biggest beneficiaries. AML, sanctions and additional agency rulemakings remain outstanding, with investor focus shifting to implementation and Treasury guidance.
